title: Calumny rejected: inherent justice not denied
source_text: XXII. Et postea multas a se calumnias amolientes testantur nos falso accusari, quasi omnem inhaerentem justitiam fidelibus negemus, eosque sola externa justitiae Christi imputatione, quae sit sine ulla interna renovatione, justificari statuamus. Cum tamen solis poenitentibus, & viva fide in Christum credentibus justitiam imputari, simulque per eandem fidem a Spiritu Sancto corda contrita vivificari, ad ardentem erga Christum charitatem & novae obedientiae studium excitari, a pravis videlicet cupiditatibus mundari, atque ita justitiam & sanctitatem vitae novae inchoari, & in dies perfici doceamus. Id tantum addimus, inquiunt, per hanc inhaerentem justitiam propriam, quia in hac vita imperfecta est, neminem coram severo Dei judicio posse consistere, aut in ea confidere, ut a reatu mortis per eam justificetur, seu absolvatur; sed per & propter solam perfectissimam Christi justitiam & meritum viva fide apprehensum.
pass_a_gloss: And afterward, clearing many calumnies from themselves, they testify that we are falsely accused as if we denied all inherent righteousness to the faithful and held that they are justified by the mere external imputation of Christ’s righteousness without any internal renovation. Whereas we teach that righteousness is imputed only to the penitent and those believing in Christ with living faith, and that at the same time by the same faith the Holy Spirit vivifies contrite hearts, stirs them to ardent charity toward Christ and zeal for new obedience, cleanses them from wicked desires, and so begins and day by day perfects the righteousness and holiness of the new life. This only we add, they say: that by this inherent righteousness of our own, because it is imperfect in this life, no one can stand before God’s severe judgment or trust in it so as to be justified or absolved from the guilt of death by it; but only through and on account of the most perfect righteousness and merit of Christ apprehended by living faith.
pass_b_english: False charge: Reformed deny all inherent justice and teach bare external imputation.
We impute only to living faith with Spirit-wrought renovation; imperfect inherent justice cannot absolve at the severe bar.
